column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  one line per deg(0) cube of the symmetry-broken encoding.
# Written by tools/rung.sh; each line is one `iota_sym --only-deg` invocation.
# The rung is UNSAT only when EVERY cube is UNSAT. A cube marked
# `undecided` carries the budget it was stopped at, per docs/reading.md rule 13.
# SIX OF THESE CUBES ARE PROVABLY EMPTY AND DID NOT NEED SOLVING.
# In a 4-uniform sunflower-free family every point has degree at most
# g(3): the star at a point IS its link, which is 3-uniform, distinct and
# sunflower-free (PureLink.link_at_point_bounded).  PureLink.g_three_at_most_26
# gives g(3) <= 26 unconditionally, so deg(0) >= 27 is impossible and
# cubes 27..32 contain nothing.  They were solved anyway, before this was
# noticed, and cadical returned UNSAT for every one -- which is a cross
# check of the encoding against the kernel rather than wasted work, but
# it was not deliberate.
# With AbbottGardner1969 (g(3) = 20) the empty range widens to 21..32 and
# only deg(0) = 12..20 can hold anything.  That value is a citation, so
# the unconditional statement is the one this file is run against.
# Cube 12 -- the floor, and the one 33.5a expected to be worst -- was
# decided on an Apple M4 Air, not on the session container: RUNG_THREADS=8
# RUNG_SLICE=900, so it stalled at 900 s, split into 19 degree-sequence
# sub-cubes and finished UNSAT at 3236.4 s with none at the limit. That
# is 33.5a's "nineteen sequences" for deficiency four, confirmed. Every
# other row was measured on the container.
# Cubes 15 and 16 were decided on the same M4-class VM, WHOLE -- run with
# RUNG_SLICE=90000 above the 86400 s budget, so the degree-sequence split
# never fired and each is one sequential cadical on one core.
# THE WHOLE-CUBE COST CURVE -- AND THE FIT THAT WAS WRONG.
# An earlier version of this header fitted a log-linear curve to the
# three points 17/16/15, got 2.89x per step down, and predicted
# deg(0)=14 came in at 51305.5 s. The prediction was HIGH BY 1.92x, and
# the ratio broke from ~2.9x to 1.47x, so the curve is not geometric and
# the fit's form was wrong rather than merely imprecise. THE 79 h FIGURE
# FOR deg(0)=13 IS WITHDRAWN; three measured ratios that do not agree
# with each other cannot support a fourth.
# What can be said instead: 13 is the last open cube, its cost is
# unknown, and the one structural fact nearby is that the number of
# admissible degree sequences falls sharply as deg(0) does --
# the whole-cube time rose from 16 to 14. Whether that trend continues
# to 13 is exactly what is not known.
# WHICH MEANS THE DEGREE-SEQUENCE SPLIT IS THE WRONG TOOL AT deg(0)=13.
# Measured this session: the split makes 1939 sub-cubes, solved ones land
# in 136-491 s and about 45% pass 600 s, so the total is roughly 597
# core-hours against 79 for the cube whole -- a factor of 7.6 the wrong
# way. The split wins only when it is small: at deg(0)=12 it is 19
# sub-cubes and it turned an undecided cube into 3236 s.
# So iota_sym's default --cubecap 400 was RIGHT to refuse the split at
# deg(0) = 13 and 14, and session N+11's diagnosis -- that the cap
# carried over from the g=10 rung was the reason those cubes failed --
# was backwards. The cap was the protection, not the bug. Raising it to
# 3000 or 4000 forces a split that costs 7.6x more than not splitting.
# deg0
